subject: Private deployment DPA: redlines for subprocessors, BYOK custody, and operator access
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medisys.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Medisys Legal <legal@medisys.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@medisys.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy DPA addendum questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks for sending over the draft addendum for private deployments. Our legal team reviewed and flagged a few items we need clarified before we can proceed:

1) Subprocessors: we need clarity on the list of subprocessors for on-prem and VPC options (are cloud providers considered subprocessors if we engage Redwood Dedicated or is this strictly for hosted?). Please provide the current list and your process for notifying and obtaining consent for new subprocessors.

2) BYOK custody: the draft implies Redwood can hold escrowed keys in exceptional circumstances. We need strict limits — who can access escrow and under what legal process? Also proposal to add a short SLA for key retrieval in incident scenarios.

3) Operator access / telemetry: we require details on what operator access looks like for customer-managed stacks (runbooks, exact telemetry collected, and any remote admin access). Can you provide a runbook stub?

We attached our redlines (pdf) and would like to schedule a short call to walk through items 1–3.

Best,
Laura Chen
Director, Procurement
Medisys Health

Attachment: Medisys-redlines-20270718.pdf (redlines summary)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medisys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy DPA addendum questions

Laura —

Thanks for the thoughtful review and the redlines. Quick replies inline below and attaching our proposed addendum (PDF) plus a 1-page operator runbook stub. Happy to hop on a call — I’m free tomorrow 10–11am PT or Tuesday afternoon.

1) Subprocessors: For Private (VPC/on-prem) the only regular subprocessor is our managed control-plane for billing/telemetry (hosted control-plane is in scope for Dedicated customers who opt in). If a customer fully self-hosts (on-prem air-gapped) there are zero Redwood subprocessors for customer data paths; we will note that explicitly. We can add an explicit subprocessor list and a 30-day notice clause for additions.

2) BYOK escrow: We do maintain an optional escrow mechanism for BYOK to support disaster recovery and key-retrieval SLAs. Access is limited to two named roles (Encryption Escrow Officer and Head of Infra Security), requires a signed owner request + two-party authorization, and is logged to an immutable audit trail (retained per DPA). We can add a 72-hour key-retrieval SLA for emergency scenarios and define legal thresholds (court order/subpoena or customer-signed retrieval request).

3) Operator access / telemetry: The runbook stub (attached) enumerates allowed operators, scopes (console-level vs. host-level), and the telemetry types (service-level logs, anonymized metrics, and optional kernel traces which are only enabled with customer consent). No remote shell access is undertaken without customer explicit breakglass approval.

I’m looping in Kar (sales) and Irene (security) to confirm the operational details and to propose precise DPA language for the escrow and subprocessor clauses.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-DPA-PrivDeploy-Addendum_v1.pdf; PrivDeploy-Operator-Runbook-stub.txt

From: Medisys Legal <legal@medisys.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medisys.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@medisys.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private deploy DPA addendum questions

Sean,

Thanks for the quick response. A few follow-ups after internal review and counsel input:

- The 30-day notice for subprocessors is acceptable only if customers may object and require compensation/termination rights. Please confirm whether Redwood would provide a termination for convenience right in that narrow window.

- The 72-hour key retrieval SLA is helpful but we need more granularity on the authorization workflow and an immutable proof-of-request record suitable for audit. Also propose a clause that escrowed keys are stored in a split-keystore (multi-party) model and require two independent Redwood approvals plus customer acknowledgement.

- Telemetry: we consider kernel traces and any host-level logs to be high-sensitivity. If those are required for support we need a secure process: ephemeral access tokens, single-use sessions, full session recordings, and retention limits.

We attached our annotated redline pdf (Medisys-redlines-20270719.pdf). Please propose DPA wording that addresses the above and confirm whether any subprocessors are located outside the US (we need mapping for cross-border risk).

Regards,
Medisys Legal

Attachment: Medisys-redlines-20270719.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@medisys.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-19T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy DPA addendum questions — proposed language

Hi all,

Following up with concrete language proposals and operational confirmations:

1) Subprocessors: Proposed clause — "For Private (VPC and on-prem) deployments, Redwood will not engage subprocessors that have access to customer plaintext data paths unless explicitly permitted in writing by the customer. For hosted control-plane services that process metadata (billing, anonymized telemetry), a current subprocessor list will be published and customers will receive 30 days' notice of additions. Customers may object within the notice period; if objection is not resolved, the customer may terminate affected services subject to a short wind-down period and refund for unused committed capacity."

2) BYOK escrow: Operational model — we will implement split-keystore escrow using a customer-held share + Redwood-held shard. Escrow access requires: (a) a customer-signed retrieval request or lawful process enforcement; (b) two Redwood Encryption Escrow Officers (names to be provided) to approve; and (c) generation of an auditable transcript (signed log). We propose a 72-hour SLA for retrieval once all authorizations are validated.

3) Operator telemetry: Proposed controls — ephemeral access tokens (maximum 4-hour session), session recording stored in write-once logs for 90 days by default (option to shorten to 30 days), and explicit customer approval for host-level traces. No persistent remote shell access without documented breakglass.

Irene — any additional security controls we should call out?

Thanks,
Kar
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@medisys.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-19T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy DPA addendum questions — security confirmation

Laura / team —

Quick technical confirmations to support Kar's language:

- Split-keystore: we'll document the shard algorithm and HSM protections in a technical appendix. Customer shard never leaves customer boundary for on-prem. For VPC where customer BYOK is used, the customer retains control over key material; Redwood-held shard alone is cryptographically useless.

- Audit trail: retrieval requests are logged to an append-only ledger (SHA256 chains) and not modifiable by ops. We can provide sample log entries for audit review.

- Cross-border: current subprocessors for hosted control-plane are US and EU-based monitoring infra (no access to plaintext). We'll provide a table mapping datacenter regions and subprocessors.

I recommend adding language that prohibits Redwood from using escrowed keys for any purpose other than retrieval authorized by the documented process; explicit criminal/legal process is required otherwise.

Happy to jump on a technical call to walk through the appendix.

—Irene
Sr. Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medisys.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-21T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy DPA addendum questions

Sean / Kar / Irene —

Thanks — the proposed wording and the security confirmations address the majority of our concerns. A few outstanding items: we need the names/titles of the two Redwood Encryption Escrow Officers and a representative sample of the retrieval audit transcript. Also please add the explicit termination-for-convenience carveout for subprocessor objections.

Can you produce the updated DPA redline (incorporating split-keystore language, the SLA, and the terminable subprocessor clause) and the sample audit transcript by Friday EOD our time? If so, we’ll schedule signoff with counsel next Monday.

Best regards,
Laura Chen
Director, Procurement
Medisys Health
